results.name: network_packet_buffer_allocate_and_copy
results.evidence: GlobalAlloc's a buffer sized param_1+2 if none given, writes a packed length/flags header into the first word, then copies param_1 bytes from the source (in_ECX) after the header; classic length-prefixed buffer builder but exact call site/consumer not visible.
results.summary: Allocates (or reuses) a small heap buffer, encodes a length+flags header in its first word, and copies the supplied data after the header.

results.name: network_random_value_generate
results.evidence: Seeds the CRT RNG once via a time32()-derived seed and FUN_006240c2 (srand-shaped call), then calls _rand() and post-processes it through FUN_006391b4 before adding an unaff_ESI base value.
results.summary: Lazily seeds the C runtime random number generator from the current time, then returns a random value offset by a caller-supplied base held in ESI.

results.name: network_mutex_slot_allocate
results.evidence: Scans a fixed 40-byte-stride table (DAT_006f0db0..006f12d4) for a free slot (flag byte == 0), zeroes the handle/name fields, marks it used, and returns a pointer whose layout (handle dword + name buffer) exactly matches what FUN_00440510 (mutex_create) fills in.
results.summary: Finds and reserves a free entry in the static mutex-record table used by the named-mutex allocator.

results.name: network_thread_create
results.evidence: Finds a free slot in a 32-entry HANDLE table, calls CreateThread, maps param_1 flag bits to a SetThreadPriority level, calls ResumeThread, and rolls back with CloseHandle on failure.
results.summary: Creates a worker thread, tracks its handle in a small internal table, applies a priority derived from flag bits, resumes it, and reports success/failure through an out parameter.

results.name: mutex_create
results.evidence: Matches naming-hint string 'mutex_%ld' exactly: allocates a slot via FUN_00440420, snprintf's the name 'mutex_%ld' with an incrementing counter, calls CreateMutexA, and returns success/handle through an out param.
results.summary: Allocates a table slot and creates a uniquely-named Win32 mutex ('mutex_<n>'), returning the handle via an output parameter.

results.name: network_address_to_string
results.evidence: Formats a network address struct into a static buffer using '%hd.%hd.%hd.%hd:%hu' when the address-family/length field (in_EAX[8]) is 4, or the 8-group hex ':%hu' format when it is 0x10, matching Blam's s_network_address (4-byte vs 16-byte address) layout.
results.summary: Converts an s_network_address structure to a human-readable 'ip:port' (or IPv6-style) string in a shared static buffer.

results.name: enum_value_to_display_char
results.evidence: Pure switch mapping input values 3,4,5,6,8 to fixed byte codes (0x37,0x38,0x39,0x2e,0x31) with default 0x2b; no strings/globals/callees to confirm the domain, so purpose (likely a UI glyph/char lookup) is a guess.
results.summary: Maps a small integer enum value to a fixed output byte via a lookup switch, purpose unconfirmed.

results.name: network_stats_summary_log_open
results.evidence: When enabled (DAT_006869bc flag), builds a timestamped '...\Game Summary <date>.xls' filename via strftime + FUN_00449250, opens it with FUN_00624186, writes the tab-separated header row, and starts a new averaging interval (FUN_00449210 stores the interval start tick).
results.summary: Opens a new tab-delimited 'Game Summary' bandwidth-statistics log file (writing its header) and resets the interval accumulators.

results.name: network_stats_summary_log_write
results.evidence: Uses the same interval-accumulator globals (DAT_0087bea0..beb8) reset by FUN_00440670 and appends one fprintf row of computed rates/bytes/packets to DAT_006a6140, then fflush's it.
results.summary: Computes per-interval bandwidth/packet statistics and appends one summary row to the open 'Game Summary' log file.

results.name: network_connection_stats_lookup_or_add
results.evidence: Linear-searches a 0xff-entry, 0x22-stride table for a record matching (unaff_EBX id, unaff_DI value); on miss it allocates the next free slot (bumping DAT_006f14bc) and zero-initializes its many per-connection counters (bec0..bf00 family), matching the fields updated by FUN_00440b20/FUN_00440d20.
results.summary: Finds the per-connection statistics record matching a given id/value pair, creating and zero-initializing a new one if none exists.

results.name: network_connection_stats_record_packet
results.evidence: Looks up the connection's stats slot via FUN_00440a80 and increments send- or receive-side byte/packet counters (bed4/bee4/bef4/befc for sent, bed8/bee8/bef8/bf00 for received) based on param_1, with extra reliable/unreliable breakdowns gated by param_2/param_3.
results.summary: Updates a connection's per-packet statistics counters (bytes/packets sent or received, including reliable/unreliable breakdowns) for one transmitted or received packet.

results.name: network_connection_stats_end
results.evidence: Looks up the connection slot via FUN_00440a80, and if marked active (bec8!=0) folds the elapsed time since bec4 into the cumulative bec0 field and clears the active flag.
results.summary: Finalizes a connection's tracked lifetime by adding the time since it became active into its cumulative duration and marking it inactive.

results.name: network_connection_stats_log_tick
results.evidence: Opens a timestamped '...\gamespy <date>.xls' log with per-connection tab-separated headers (strings match exactly), then every 100ms dumps one row per tracked connection (DAT_0087bee4 table) and accumulates ping-like values from a linked list (DAT_0071c2d8/DAT_0071c2d4) into DAT_0087beb4/beb8.
results.summary: Periodically (every 100ms) opens/writes a per-connection 'gamespy' traffic log, one row per active connection, and rolls those per-connection stats back into the overall averages.

results.name: network_channels_open
results.evidence: Builds two local addresses via FUN_006148b0 from DAT_006869b0 (local IP) and two port globals, then creates the game-data and gamespy/query channels (thunk_FUN_0061c3e0) storing handles in DAT_006f14c4/DAT_006f14c8, wiring up callbacks with FUN_0061e550/FUN_00614850/FUN_00614800.
results.summary: Creates and binds the two main UDP network channels (game data and query) if they are not already open, wiring up their receive/error callbacks.

results.name: network_channels_close
results.evidence: Closes DAT_006f14c8 and DAT_006f14c4 via FUN_00614860 (the same close routine used elsewhere on channel handles) and zeroes both globals.
results.summary: Closes both of the module's main network channel handles and clears their globals.

results.name: network_game_initialize
results.evidence: Calls FUN_004415c0 (winsock/network startup) and, on success, sets default rate/flag globals; separately registers the game message dispatch table via FUN_004d0980(&PTR_s_network_game_messages_group_006994f8) the first time DAT_007196ec is zero.
results.summary: Initializes networking (winsock etc.) and, on first run, registers the network game-message dispatch group used to route incoming gameplay packets.

results.name: network_hostname_thread_proc
results.evidence: Calls gethostname(param_1, 0x100), sets a completion flag (DAT_006f14cc), and terminates via ExitThread(0); used as the CreateThread routine in FUN_00441540.
results.summary: Thread entry point that retrieves the local machine's hostname into a buffer, signals completion, and exits the thread.

results.name: network_local_hostent_get
results.evidence: Spawns FUN_00441510 (gethostname thread) with a timeout via WaitForSingleObject/TerminateThread, then on success calls gethostbyname on the retrieved name and returns the hostent pointer through *param_1.
results.summary: Resolves and returns the local machine's hostent structure, retrieving the hostname on a watchdog-timed worker thread first.

results.name: network_initialize
results.evidence: Performs WSAStartup, resolves/derives the local IP (via configured DAT_006869b0 or FUN_00441540 hostname lookup), starts the main network worker thread (FUN_005771c0), and records the startup tick via FUN_00449210, guarded by the DAT_006869b8 'initialized' flag.
results.summary: One-time networking subsystem startup: calls WSAStartup, determines the local IP address, and launches the background network processing thread.

results.name: network_shutdown
results.evidence: Guarded by DAT_006869b8, closes both channel handles, closes the bandwidth summary log, and if the per-connection ('gamespy') log is open writes final per-connection and aggregate totals ('Connection [%d] ... Log file closed') before fclose'ing it.
results.summary: Tears down the networking subsystem: closes channels, flushes and closes both statistics log files with final summary lines, and clears the initialized flag.

results.name: network_update
results.evidence: Uses QueryPerformanceCounter plus __allmul/__alldiv to compute a scaled current time into DAT_006a6144, then calls the per-connection log tick (FUN_00440d80) and services both channels (FUN_00614540) once per call.
results.summary: Per-frame networking service routine: updates the high-resolution clock, drives the connection-statistics log, and pumps both network channels.

results.name: network_channel_list_new
results.evidence: Allocates a 0x114-byte header via GlobalAlloc and, if the requested count (in_AX) is under 65, allocates a parallel dword array (GlobalAlloc(0x40,count*4)) and initializes count/head fields at offsets 0x104/0x108/0x10c/0x110 - the same offsets read by FUN_004419d0 (unaff_EDI+0x104/0x10c).
results.summary: Allocates a small fixed-capacity array/queue container object (pointer array plus header fields) used to track a bounded set of network channels.

results.name: network_channel_list_poll
results.evidence: Walks the array at unaff_EDI+0x104 up to unaff_EDI+0x10c entries, and for each channel checks either a 'ready' flag byte or computes a ring-buffer fill level (read/write offsets at +8/+0xc/+0x10) to decide if data is pending, setting bit 4 on the channel when so.
results.summary: Iterates a channel list, marking each channel that has data ready to read (either explicitly flagged or via a nonzero circular-buffer fill level).

results.name: network_channel_list_add
results.evidence: Stores the new channel pointer into the array at in_ECX[0x41] (bounds-checked against in_ECX[0x42]/[0x43]), then maintains a Winsock fd_set-shaped unique-value list (count at in_ECX[0], up to 64 values at in_ECX[1..0x40]) keyed on a value from the channel (offset 8), finally OR's flag bit 0x8 onto the channel.
results.summary: Adds a channel to a bounded (fd_set-style) channel list, deduplicating it in an accompanying up-to-64-entry key array, and marks the channel as 'in list'.

results.name: network_channel_list_remove
results.evidence: Finds the matching channel pointer in the array, removes its key from the same fd_set-style unique-value array (shifting subsequent entries down), swaps the last array slot into the found index, decrements the count, and clears flag bit 0x8 on the channel (mirrors FUN_00441a40's add logic).
results.summary: Removes a channel from the bounded channel list and its associated key-dedup array, clearing the channel's 'in list' flag.

results.name: network_handle_table_cleanup
results.evidence: Iterates a global table of (HANDLE, flag) pairs from DAT_006f14d0 to DAT_006f16d0 (stride 8) and CloseHandle's + zeroes any entry whose flag is set.
results.summary: Closes and clears any outstanding handles left in a fixed-size global handle/flag table.

results.name: network_receive_queue_new
results.evidence: Resets channel/handle state (FUN_00441300, FUN_00441bb0) then allocates a 0x1c-byte wrapper plus an inner 0x10019-byte buffer object stamped with the 'circ' magic tag and the name string 'received_data_queue', matching the naming hint that ties this cluster to a circular_buffer implementation.
results.summary: Constructs the network receive-queue object: a small header wrapping a large tagged circular buffer named 'received_data_queue'.

results.name: network_receive_queue_free
results.evidence: Mirrors FUN_00441bf0's construction: tears down the channel referenced by the wrapper (FUN_006175f0/FUN_006147d0/FUN_00440d20/FUN_00614830), frees the inner circular-buffer object and the wrapper itself via GlobalFree, then cleans up the handle table (FUN_00441bb0).
results.summary: Destroys a network receive-queue object created by FUN_00441bf0: closes its channel, frees the inner buffer and the wrapper, and cleans up handles.

results.name: network_channel_get_remote_address
results.evidence: Reads 4 address bytes and a port either from a per-object channel (if FUN_006147a0 reports type 1) or from the fallback global channel DAT_006f14c4, and writes them into an output struct at the exact offsets (dword addr, +0x12 port, +4*4=+16 family=4) matching the s_network_address layout used by FUN_00440570.
results.summary: Fills an s_network_address structure with the remote IPv4 address and port of a channel (or of the shared fallback channel), reporting an error code if neither is available.

results.name: network_channel_receive_callback
results.evidence: Looks up the channel object via FUN_00614840; if its 'connectionless' flag (bit0) is clear it captures/formats the sender address (FUN_006175f0/FUN_006147d0/FUN_006148b0), otherwise for a connection-oriented channel with data it forwards the payload straight into circular_buffer_write.
results.summary: Per-channel data-received handler: records the sender's address for connectionless channels, or appends the payload to the channel's receive circular buffer for connection-oriented ones.

results.name: network_channel_reconnect
results.evidence: Reopens the channel pair (FUN_00441300), selects DAT_006f14c8 or DAT_006f14c4 based on param_2, attempts FUN_006145a0 on it, and on failure marks the channel disconnected, sets a UI/status code (DAT_00718fa4, DAT_0071c2de) and calls FUN_004aa900 (likely a disconnect notification), returning error 0xfff0.
results.summary: Attempts to (re)establish a network channel connection, flagging a disconnect/error state and notifying elsewhere if the attempt fails.

results.name: network_channel_teardown
results.evidence: Deregisters the shared listening channel's callback (thunk_FUN_0061c660(DAT_006f14c4,0)) when the object's flag byte is set, then closes its own channel handle (FUN_006147a0/FUN_00614710) and clears state, mirroring the field layout used across the 0x441xxx channel-object functions.
results.summary: Tears down a single channel object: unregisters it from the listening channel if needed, closes its handle, and resets its fields.

results.name: network_listen_connection_request_handler
results.evidence: Registered as the callback for the listening channel (see FUN_00442170: thunk_FUN_0061c660(DAT_006f14c4, FUN_00442090)); on invocation it queues the incoming request's address/port/callback info into the bounded (0x1e/30-slot) DAT_0087bc20 table indexed by DAT_006f16d0, and reports a status code back to the caller via thunk_FUN_0061cee0.
results.summary: Callback invoked when a connection request arrives on the listening channel; queues the pending request (up to 30 outstanding) for later accept/reject.

results.name: network_listen_start
results.evidence: Marks the local listen-state flag, calls FUN_00614810 on DAT_006f14c4, sets flag bit 0x2 on the object, and registers FUN_00442090 as the channel's event callback via thunk_FUN_0061c660.
results.summary: Puts the shared network channel into a listening state and installs the incoming-connection-request callback.

results.name: network_listen_accept_pending_connection
results.evidence: When the pending-request queue (DAT_006f16d0) is non-empty, calls thunk_FUN_0061ce80 to accept the queued request, and on success constructs a receive-queue object via FUN_00441bf0, links it to the channel (FUN_00614830), sets flag bit 0x1, and fills its address via FUN_00441ce0/FUN_00440570.
results.summary: Pops the most recent pending incoming connection request from the queue and, if it can be accepted, builds a fully-initialized channel/receive-queue object for it.

results.name: network_listen_reject_pending_connection
results.evidence: When the pending-request queue (DAT_006f16d0) is non-empty, rejects/cancels the most recent queued entry via thunk_FUN_0061cee0 and decrements the queue count, mirroring FUN_004421b0's accept path.
results.summary: Cancels (rejects) the most recently queued pending incoming connection request without accepting it.

results.name: master_server_query_tick
results.evidence: State-machine tick over a bitmask (DAT_0071969c) driving distinct master-server operations: server-list query (FUN_00617290 over DAT_007196bc), heartbeat send (FUN_006171d0/FUN_006171a0 chosen by DAT_006953f0), and single-server refresh, each guarded by a mutex (WaitForSingleObject/ReleaseMutex on DAT_007196a8).
results.summary: Background master-server processing tick: services pending server-list queries, heartbeats, and single-server refresh requests indicated by a request flag bitmask.

results.name: master_server_connection_start
results.evidence: Resets connection state globals, calls the confirmed mutex_create (FUN_00440510) then network_thread_create (FUN_00440460) with routine 'sig__setup_master_server_connection_sig', storing the thread handle in DAT_007196ac; rolls back the mutex handle on thread-create failure.
results.summary: Creates the mutex and background worker thread that establish the master-server connection, cleaning up on failure.

results.name: master_server_connection_wait
results.evidence: Polls the connection thread (DAT_007196ac) with GetExitCodeThread in a Sleep(20) loop, periodically invoking FUN_00549960 (likely a UI progress pump) using a QueryPerformanceCounter-based interval, then closes both the thread and mutex handles once the thread exits.
results.summary: Waits for the master-server connection worker thread to finish, periodically pumping a UI update, then cleans up its handles.

results.name: network_get_ticker_label_string
results.evidence: Looks up the tag 'ui\shell\main_menu\multiplayer_type_select\join_game\join_game_ticker_labels', retrieves a string-list entry via FUN_005578c0, and copies it into the caller's buffer with wcsncpy, indexed by an implicit register argument (called as FUN_004b6160(4) elsewhere).
results.summary: Copies one of the localized 'join game' ticker status strings (selected by index) from a tag's string list into the caller's buffer.

results.name: server_browser_ui_configure_widgets
results.evidence: Walks a chain of sibling UI widgets (offset 0x2c = next) toggling visible/enabled byte pairs at offsets 0x10/0x12 based on param_1, and pushes numeric filter settings (DAT_006953fa/fb, DAT_00719490, DAT_0071948d/e/f) into widget value fields at offset 0x40/0x48, consistent with this engine's list_item/dialog widget layout.
results.summary: Configures the visibility and value fields of a chain of server-browser filter UI widgets, switching between two display modes (e.g. internet vs LAN).

results.name: server_list_reset
results.evidence: Zeroes the server-list scroll/selection globals (DAT_00719478 scroll offset, DAT_006953f4 selection reset to -1, etc.), calls FUN_004ba7c0, then three FUN_004b8a60 calls with mode arguments 2/1/0 that mirror the UI-refresh helper FUN_004b73a0.
results.summary: Clears the server-browser's list state (selection, scroll position) and refreshes its associated UI display elements.

results.name: master_server_list_refresh_request
results.evidence: Sets bit 0x8 in the master-server request bitmask (DAT_0071969c, the same field consumed by FUN_004b5d70's tick function), computes a QueryPerformanceCounter-based 10-second timeout into DAT_006953fc, and sets the busy flag DAT_00719488.
results.summary: Requests a server-list refresh from the master server by setting a pending-request flag and a 10-second timeout deadline.

results.name: master_server_list_connect_or_refresh
results.evidence: Checks the list channel's connection state via FUN_00616ff0; if idle it tries to begin connecting (FUN_00617030), falling back to the refresh-timer path (FUN_004b6660) on failure, otherwise sets a 'connecting' bit and a 9999 timeout marker.
results.summary: Ensures the master-server list connection is established or being (re)connected, scheduling a retry if the connection attempt cannot start.

results.name: master_server_select_server_for_join
results.evidence: Under the connection mutex, validates the current selection index (DAT_006953f4) against the server list count, caches the selected server handle in DAT_00719450, checks its 'password' key via FUN_006174d0, and if set opens a password prompt (FUN_004a89a0) before flagging a pending join.
results.summary: Latches the currently selected server-list entry as the join target, prompting for a password first if the server requires one.

results.name: server_list_row_set_fields
results.evidence: Sets checkbox-style UI widget bytes (offset 0x10/0x58) from boolean parameters, and populates player-name/rank text fields via heap_reallocate+_wcsncpy plus a '%d / %d' players ratio and a clamped ping/'%d'-style value, matching a per-row server/player list entry.
results.summary: Populates one server/player list UI row's text and checkbox fields (name, player ratio, ping) from the supplied values.

results.name: server_browser_populate_server_info_row
results.evidence: Reads server-info fields (hostname/mapname/gametype/etc., matching the referenced key strings) via FUN_006174d0/FUN_00617490/FUN_00617c10, resolves the friendly map name (map_list_get_friendly_level_name), and forwards everything to FUN_004b67e0 to populate the row's UI widgets.
results.summary: Gathers one server's queried info fields (name, map, player counts, ping range) and hands them to the row-population routine for display.

results.name: server_list_compare_string_field
results.evidence: Generic qsort-style comparator: fetches a string field from each of two entries via FUN_00617490, compares with __stricmp, and inverts the result based on the DAT_006953f8 sort-direction flag; the specific field key is passed in a register not captured by the decompiler.
results.summary: Sort comparator that compares a string field (key supplied by the caller) between two server-list entries, honoring the current sort direction.

results.name: server_list_compare_by_mapname
results.evidence: Looks up the 'mapname' field on both entries, resolves each to its friendly level name via map_list_get_friendly_level_name, and wcscmp's the results, inverted by the DAT_006953f8 sort-direction flag.
results.summary: Sort comparator that orders two server-list entries by their (friendly) map name, honoring the current sort direction.

results.name: server_list_compare_by_ping_then_hostname
results.evidence: Primarily compares a numeric field via FUN_00617c10 (defaulting unset values to 9999, consistent with a ping value), then falls back to comparing the 'hostname' string field and finally raw pointer order for a stable sort, all honoring DAT_006953f8's direction flag.
results.summary: Sort comparator that orders server-list entries primarily by a numeric field (likely ping) and falls back to hostname, then entry order, as tie-breakers.

results.name: server_list_compare_by_mapname_then_hostname
results.evidence: Delegates to FUN_004b6c20 (mapname comparator) first, and only if that reports equality falls back to comparing the 'hostname' string field, both honoring DAT_006953f8's sort direction.
results.summary: Sort comparator that orders server-list entries by map name, breaking ties by hostname.

results.name: server_browser_server_passes_filter
results.evidence: Reads a server's numplayers/maxplayers/ping range, dedicated/password/teamplay flags, and gametype string, rejecting it against the current filter globals (DAT_0071948b dedicated-only, DAT_006953f9/fa/fb not-full/not-empty toggles, DAT_00719490 ping cap, and a gametype match against literal 'CTF'/'Slayer'/'Oddball'/'King'/'Race' strings), finally checking a teamplay/demo-map condition via sig__load_multiplayer_maps_demo_sig.
results.summary: Determines whether a queried server entry satisfies all of the server-browser's active filter settings (player count, ping, password, gametype, teamplay, dedicated).

results.name: server_list_scroll_position_clamp
results.evidence: Computes an effective server count (either from in_EAX or FUN_004ba820) and clamps the scroll offset DAT_00719478 into [0, count-15].
results.summary: Clamps the server-browser list's current scroll offset to stay within the valid range for the current server count.

results.name: server_browser_ui_refresh_display
results.evidence: Calls the same three FUN_004b8a60(...) UI-update invocations (modes 2, 1, and message-text) used inside FUN_004b65f0's list reset, without touching the underlying state globals.
results.summary: Refreshes the server-browser's on-screen list/header/status UI elements without altering the underlying list state.

results.name: server_browser_player_list_populate
results.evidence: Reads the 'numplayers' field, clears the player list UI (FUN_004b8a60(0,0)), then for each player fetches name/score via FUN_00617530 and formats '  %s %d     ' or '  %S %S     ' before adding each row with FUN_004b8a60.
results.summary: Populates the server-browser's per-player list UI with each player's name and score, one formatted row per player.

results.name: server_browser_game_variant_description_populate
results.evidence: Clears a UI element (FUN_004b8a60(0,1)) then, given a valid entry, reads game-variant/fraglimit-related fields (matching the referenced 'game_flags'/'gamevariant'/'fraglimit' strings) and builds a description via FUN_00557990/FUN_004b8da0.
results.summary: Builds and displays a text description of the selected server's game variant / fraglimit settings in the server-browser UI.

results.name: server_browser_open
results.evidence: Initializes networking (FUN_00441300, FUN_004b6000), resets list state (FUN_004b65f0), sets up a LAN broadcast target (FUN_0057e1a0/FUN_00576e60), loads a ticker label (FUN_004b6160), restores or defaults filter settings into the widget/global fields also touched by FUN_004b7d80/FUN_004b61c0, sets initial UI widget focus states, and calls FUN_004b80f0 to kick off the initial list population.
results.summary: Entry point that opens the multiplayer server-browser screen: starts networking/master-server connection, restores filter settings, configures the initial UI widget states, and begins listing servers.

results.name: server_list_scroll_page_up
results.evidence: Decrements the scroll offset DAT_00719478 by 14 rows (or to 0 on a 'home' flag), clamps it against the server count via FUN_004ba820, sets a negative scroll-direction marker (DAT_00719484 = -16), and updates whether the current selection is still on-screen.
results.summary: Scrolls the server list up by one page (or jumps to the top), reclamping the view and updating whether the selection is still visible.

results.name: server_list_scroll_page_down
results.evidence: Mirrors FUN_004b7b20: increments the scroll offset by 14 rows (or jumps to the bottom via FUN_004ba820 on the 'end' flag), clamps it, sets a positive scroll-direction marker (DAT_00719484 = 0x10), and updates selection visibility.
results.summary: Scrolls the server list down by one page (or jumps to the bottom), reclamping the view and updating whether the selection is still visible.

results.name: server_browser_filter_widget_clicked
results.evidence: Identifies which widget in a sibling chain (iVar1..iVar7, matching the traversal pattern used elsewhere for this dialog) was activated and toggles the matching filter boolean (DAT_006953f9/DAT_0071948b/DAT_0071948c) or the 5-way gametype radio state (DAT_00719489 selecting among the same CTF/Slayer/Oddball/King/Race options checked in FUN_004b7080), then forces a refresh (FUN_00498e90, DAT_007196c8=9999).
results.summary: Handles a click on one of the server-browser's filter checkboxes/radio buttons (including the 5-way gametype selector), toggling the corresponding filter state and forcing a list refresh.
